summary: Build a production-ready multilingual hyperlocal services platform named “AREA WORKARS” (always uppercase) connecting (1) people searching for workers, (2) workers listing services, and (3) businesses posting job requirements. Mobile-first, premium colorful corporate-but-rural-friendly UI. Search by area/pincode and by free-text skill tags; browse categories with meaningful local SVG icons, view worker cards with direct Call/WhatsApp (no booking). Includes worker registration (with Skills/Work Tags), public job request posting + job board. Worker registrations become publicly visible immediately after submission (no admin approval / no pending state); workers are stored in a public collection "workers" with status=active by default. Bilingual everywhere with Tamil as primary line and English as secondary smaller line shown below (no language switch).
architectural_notes: Brand style: trustworthy, simple, rural+urban friendly; not corporate, not ecommerce; community-service feel
Color palette: dark green + white + light grey; emphasize accessibility and readability
Typography: clean, readable font that supports both Tamil and English well
Core UX: mobile-first; no booking system; no user login required; direct Call and WhatsApp contact
Information architecture: Home (search + category grid) -> Category listing pages with worker cards; separate Worker Registration page; simple Admin panel
Worker card fields: photo, name, work type, area, experience (years), availability, Call button (green), WhatsApp button
Worker registration fields: name, phone number, work category dropdown, area, experience, working time, upload photo; after submit show 'We will verify and publish your number' message
Branding: Platform name must be “AREA WORKARS” (uppercase) everywhere; keep all other UI/UX unchanged.

Icon rendering requirement (strict fix): do not load icons via any URL/path (/assets, /public, external). Do not use . Do not use dynamic string/icon-name mapping. Each category must import and render its SVG React component directly (e.g., import ConstructionIcon from "@/icons/ConstructionIcon" and render ), with a manual hard map for the 8 main categories to ensure offline reliability.

Skill Tags: Worker Registration includes a comma-separated “Skills / Work Tags” input; on submit normalize tags (trim, lowercase, remove duplicates) and store as an array; search must match query against category, subcategory, worker name, and tags (simple contains match; accept Tamil + English); render tags on worker cards as rounded #badges; keep UI simple with no additional filters.
known_issues: App crash showing "Something went wrong" (observed after adding categories); likely caused by missing/invalid category/subcategory relations or unhandled API errors.
Broken/missing images/icons on the site; need local SVG icons for all categories/subcategories with a fallback icon when missing.
Broken image placeholders are visible on category icons; must use local SVG icons only with a fallback icon when missing.

Language direction mismatch risk: current multilingual approach (English-first with state-selected regional language) conflicts with the new requirement (Tamil-first + English second everywhere, no switch).
Many icons are missing/broken across the UI (user reports multiple icon issues).
Tamil subtitle/second-line text is not appearing in many places where bilingual labels are expected (user reports missing Tamil in many UI areas).
Duplicate categories/subcategories appear (same category shown 2–3 times); needs deduplication to avoid confusion.
Raw placeholder/i18n keys (e.g., home.hero.title, categories.construction) are visible in the UI; must be replaced with proper bilingual Tamil + English labels and never shown to users.
Regression: after last update, category/subcategory text labels reverted to raw i18n keys (e.g., category.homeservices, category.events) indicating broken label mapping/translation key resolution.

Category icons are not loading and all cards are showing the fallback icon (likely due to public assets placement, icon path mapping, filename/case-sensitivity mismatches, or incorrect import/loading method).

Frontend: Implement a fast, mobile-friendly live suggestions dropdown under the search input while typing (on the Home page and the Search Results page). Fetch suggestions instantly from the backend suggestions API, display them in a tap-friendly list, and when a suggestion is tapped, navigate to the results page using the universal text search param (to: '/search', search: { q: <suggestion> }). Do not add any filter UI.

When the user opens the site (Home page), request browser geolocation permission (GPS) and, if permission is granted, automatically fetch and display a simple mobile-friendly list of nearby approved workers sorted by nearest first, with a small helper text that reads exactly: "Showing workers near you". If permission is denied or unavailable, do not show the nearby list and let the existing area/pincode and text search flows continue to work as-is.

Extend the Worker data model to store optional geolocation coordinates captured at worker registration time, and update the worker registration submission flow to include coordinates when available (without adding any new required user-facing form fields). Ensure the system remains upgrade-safe under the conditional migration policy by migrating existing stored workers to the new schema with coordinates unset.

Update the worker result card UI (frontend/src/components/workers/WorkerCard.tsx) so each card clearly shows the following fields in this order: (1) Name (bold), (2) Work types / tags rendered as hashtag-style badges (e.g., “#plumbing”, “#cleaning”), (3) Area, (4) Distance (only when user location and worker location are available), (5) a large tap-friendly Phone button labeled “Call”, and (6) a large tap-friendly WhatsApp button labeled “Chat”.

Restyle the worker cards to match the requested mobile-friendly card design: rounded corners, light shadow, and large tap-friendly buttons, while keeping the overall page layout (grid/list/grouping) unchanged.

Add distance rendering support on search results by obtaining the user’s current browser geolocation (non-blocking) on the Worker Search Results page (frontend/src/pages/WorkerSearchResultsPage.tsx) and passing the user coordinates into WorkerCard so it can compute and display distance when possible.

Update the /search empty state so that when no workers are found, the page shows the exact message: "No workers found in this area" and also renders a set of nearby category suggestions (tap-friendly) that let the user quickly run a new search by category.

Ensure the worker result card and empty state changes remain fast-loading and safe: avoid runtime crashes when optional fields are missing (skills, area, phone, location, photo) and avoid expensive re-renders while typing/searching.

Update the worker card UI (frontend/src/components/workers/WorkerCard.tsx) to prioritize a 2-second hiring decision with this exact information order: (1) Worker name (large, bold), (2) main skill (single highlighted skill), (3) other skills as small tag badges, (4) area location, (5) availability text rendered as one of: "Available today", "Busy", or "Call to confirm" (use safe fallback to "Call to confirm" when no availability data exists). Keep the card mobile-first, uncluttered, and highly readable.

Change worker card actions to match the required hiring flow: make WhatsApp the primary action (large, green button) and Call the secondary action (outline style). Update button labels to be driven by the existing i18n system (no hardcoded visible strings) and keep the actions disabled when phone is missing.

Add quick trust indicators to worker cards: show a "Verified number" indicator when the worker is verified, and show a "Recently active" indicator when recent activity data is available; ensure both indicators render safely and do not overcrowd the card. All indicator labels must be sourced from the existing i18n system.

When displaying many workers on the search results page (frontend/src/pages/WorkerSearchResultsPage.tsx), sort workers by relevance in this strict priority order: (1) tag match, (2) area match, (3) recent activity. Apply this sorting to both universal text-search results and category/area search results before rendering, while preserving existing grouping behavior (when grouping is enabled, sorting must happen within each group).

Add/extend i18n translation keys for the new worker-card-specific labels introduced by this change (including: "Main skill", "Other skills", "Availability", the 3 availability values, "Verified number", "Recently active"), and ensure all new visible strings used by the worker card and search results sorting/trust UI are resolved via useI18n().

Replace the current static /search empty state UI in frontend/src/pages/WorkerSearchResultsPage.tsx with a mobile-first “smart recovery” flow that always gives the user a clear next action instead of leaving them stuck.

In the /search empty state, display a friendly message using the exact Tamil text provided by the user, and source it via the existing i18n system (useI18n().t) so it can render as bilingual text (Tamil primary + English secondary) without hardcoded inline strings.
In the /search empty state, automatically show a list of nearby approved workers when browser geolocation is available, without requiring additional user input.

Add an “Expand Search Area” secondary action in the /search empty state that increases the nearby search radius and refreshes the nearby workers section accordingly (only when geolocation is available).

In the /search empty state, show “related skill suggestions” based on the user’s current search (prefer q when present; otherwise category/subcategory/area context). Suggestions must be tap-friendly and start a new /search?q=<suggestion> search when tapped.

Add two big action buttons to the /search empty state: (1) Primary: “Post a Work Request” which navigates to the existing job request page route (/post-job); (2) Secondary: “Expand Search Area” (covered separately) with large, mobile-friendly styling.
Add a WhatsApp help CTA to the /search empty state, showing the exact Tamil prompt text provided by the user (sourced via i18n), and render a WhatsApp button that opens a WhatsApp chat/help link.

Ensure that the empty state recovery UI never renders technical category/taxonomy codes (e.g., "homeimprovement", "specializedcleaning") anywhere in visible text; all category/subcategory/suggestion labels shown in the empty-state flow must be human-readable and should use the existing bilingual label helpers / i18n lookups with safe humanized fallbacks.

Extend the local i18n translation dictionary (frontend/src/components/i18n/translations.ts) with keys needed for the new empty-state recovery flow (friendly message, section labels, button labels, WhatsApp prompt), and ensure they resolve through useI18n().t without showing raw keys.

Fix the global CSS/Tailwind styling regression so the UI no longer renders like plain HTML, restoring the intended design system: light background, rounded cards, soft shadows, consistent spacing, and mobile-first layout across all pages.

Fix global CSS loading so global styles are imported exactly once and reliably applied: ensure the app’s global stylesheet (index.css / globals.css equivalent) is loaded from the root entry and not duplicated or omitted.
Force a light theme and remove any dark-mode fallback behavior so the UI always uses the light color tokens regardless of system preference or any lingering 'dark' class on the document/root.

Update the global page container to a strict mobile-first centered layout: max-width 480px, horizontally centered, with 16px padding, and apply it consistently to page content (including header/footer alignment).

Replace the current header navigation with the required minimal header: left side shows 'AREA WORKARS' as green logo text; right side shows a hamburger menu icon. Remove the desktop top navigation buttons and ensure the header does NOT show 'Browse Workers', 'Post Job', 'Blog', or 'Admin' as visible navigation items.

Implement a mobile drawer menu triggered by the hamburger icon and ensure navigation links removed from the header bar are not shown as visible menu items (specifically do not display: 'Browse Workers', 'Post Job', 'Blog', 'Admin').
Restore the Home page category grid styling to a 2-column responsive card grid with equal-height cards, centered icons, and bilingual labels with English on top and Tamil directly below.
Standardize primary button styling across the UI: green primary buttons, rounded corners, and fixed height of 48px (including key CTAs such as search submit buttons and primary form actions).

Increase the visual spacing between the category cards in the Home page Categories grid (frontend/src/pages/HomePage.tsx), by adjusting only the Tailwind grid gap values (currently `gap-4 md:gap-6`) so the cards have more whitespace between them on mobile and desktop.

Update the Worker Card UI (frontend/src/components/workers/WorkerCard.tsx) to include a 3-action direct contact system for every worker profile: (1) Call button, (2) WhatsApp button, and (3) Send job request button, using a mobile-first layout with large, rounded, easy-to-tap buttons suitable for non-technical users.

Implement WhatsApp deep-linking from worker cards so that clicking WhatsApp opens WhatsApp with the worker’s number and a prefilled message exactly:
"Hello, I found you on AREA WORKARS. I need work for [category] in [area]. Please contact me.".
Replace [category] and [area] using the best available context (prefer current search context if available; otherwise fall back to the worker’s own category/area fields), and URL-encode the message safely.

Wire the new “Send job request” action on the Worker Card to navigate to the existing job request page route (/post-job) and prefill the Job Request form fields for Work Type and Area based on the same [category] and [area] context used for the WhatsApp prefilled message.

Extend the local i18n translation dictionary (frontend/src/components/i18n/translations.ts) with any missing keys needed for the new Worker Card action label “Send job request” and for the WhatsApp prefilled-message template (if implemented via i18n), ensuring the UI does not render raw i18n keys.

Fix TanStack Router setup in frontend/src/App.tsx so the app renders routes correctly in production (no blank white screen), by removing the nested/recursive RouterProvider usage inside the root route layout and using the proper root-route outlet rendering pattern while keeping the existing HeaderBar/FooterBar layout and all styling unchanged.

Eliminate conflicting React Query provider setup that could contribute to runtime instability by ensuring there is a single QueryClientProvider in the render tree (frontend/src/main.tsx already wraps the app). Update frontend/src/App.tsx to stop creating/wrapping a second QueryClientProvider, without changing any query behavior or UI.

Add a minimal, non-design-changing runtime safety net to prevent a total blank page when HomePage or worker list rendering hits unexpected runtime errors: ensure the route render path fails gracefully (e.g., safe fallback UI within the existing layout container) and logs errors, without introducing new product features or changing the intended design.

Fix the Home page category-card icon source mapping so each main category card renders its correct icon instead of always resolving to the fallback icon, without changing any layout, spacing, styling, or card structure.

Audit and correct the icon loading implementation so it loads the correct local static assets reliably in production builds: verify filenames and exact case under the public assets folder, verify the referenced icon paths match actual filenames, and ensure the icon import/loading method used by the category cards matches the asset location strategy (public-path string vs imported component).

Fix SafeIconImage fallback configuration so that when a category icon fails to load it falls back to an existing local fallback asset (and does not point to a non-existent file extension), while keeping the component’s rendered markup and styling behavior unchanged.

Update the worker card component (frontend/src/components/workers/WorkerCard.tsx) to show exactly two direct-contact action buttons: Call and WhatsApp (no additional actions). The buttons must be rendered as two rounded buttons side-by-side, mobile-friendly, and visually sticky at the bottom of the card (i.e., pinned to the card bottom within the card layout even when other content height varies).

Implement the required contact behaviors on WorkerCard actions: Call must open the device dialer via a tel: link using the worker phone number; WhatsApp must open a wa.me link using the worker phone number. Ensure phone numbers are safely sanitized for wa.me (digits-only) and the UI remains safe when phone is missing.

Add/adjust i18n translations so the WorkerCard action button labels resolve via the existing i18n system keys (no hardcoded visible strings) and render as bilingual labels with English + Tamil for: Call and WhatsApp. Ensure the Tamil for Call is exactly "அழைக்க" and the Tamil for WhatsApp is exactly "வாட்ஸ்அப்".
Create a new mobile-first Worker Profile View page that displays a single worker’s information with a clean card layout and bilingual (Tamil + English) field labels.
Update the worker browsing flow so clicking a WorkerCard opens the Worker Profile View page for that worker, without breaking the existing Call/WhatsApp buttons.
Implement a frontend data-loading flow for the Worker Profile View page that fetches a worker by id and renders safe loading and not-found states without requiring login.
Add sticky bottom action buttons on the Worker Profile View page: Call and WhatsApp, using the same direct-contact behavior as WorkerCard (tel: and wa.me with sanitized phone numbers).

Extend the local i18n dictionary with keys needed for Worker Profile View labels (e.g., Name, Work, Area, Experience, Work description, Available time, Languages spoken) so the profile page never shows raw keys.
Keep the Worker Profile View page aligned with product constraints: no login requirement, no payment, and no booking/chat flows—only direct contact.

Update the local i18n translation dictionary so the Worker Registration form field label keys and placeholder keys currently showing raw strings (e.g., "register.field.name", "register.placeholder.name") resolve to real readable text in both English and Tamil, using exactly these label translations:
- Name / பெயர்
- Phone Number / தொலைபேசி எண்
- Category / பணி வகை
- Sub Category / உப வகை
- Area / பகுதி
- Experience / அனுபவம்
- Description / விவரம்
Also add/adjust placeholder translations for these same fields so placeholders are readable text (not keys) and align with the above wording.

Harden the i18n lookup so missing translations never return a user-visible raw key string. When a translation key is missing, return a human-readable fallback (English + Tamil) instead of the original key (e.g., never render values containing dotted key patterns like "register.field.name" anywhere in the UI).

Implement a single display-label formatter for category strings (and any other taxonomy-like strings shown to users) that converts slugs/camelCase into human-readable Title Case, with explicit overrides for the provided slugs, without changing any stored database values.

Apply the category display-label formatter everywhere category/subcategory values can be visible to the user, ensuring raw database slugs are never shown in: (1) Home page category cards, (2) Search results page title and any category/subcategory labels, (3) Worker cards, (4) Worker profile page work/type badge, and (5) Live suggestions dropdown + empty-state suggestion buttons; keep the underlying values used for navigation/search unchanged.

Create a centralized frontend-only `displayName` formatter function for taxonomy-like strings (category/subcategory/group/skills) that converts database slugs/camelCase into human-readable Title Case labels without changing any stored values or navigation/search params. The formatter must follow these rules: (1) split joined words where possible, (2) insert spaces before capital letters, (3) convert to Title Case, and (4) never allow a raw slug to be shown in the UI. It must satisfy these examples exactly: `homeimprovement` -> `Home Improvement`, `specializedcleaning` -> `Specialized Cleaning`, `securityservices` -> `Security Services`, `vehicleServices` -> `Vehicle Services`.

Apply `displayName` everywhere category/subcategory/taxonomy values can be user-visible, ensuring that raw database values like `Homeimprovement` and `Specializedcleaning` never render anywhere in the UI. This must include at minimum: Home page category cards (title + any subtitle), search suggestions dropdown display text, worker profile page work/type badge and any other taxonomy-derived labels, and all filter UI labels/chips/titles on the search results page.

Create a strict, centralized category display-label mapping system in the frontend by introducing a `CATEGORY_LABELS` dictionary that maps category slugs to human-readable labels, and a single helper function that UI code must call to render category labels. The dictionary must include (at minimum) the exact mappings provided by the user: construction→Construction, agriculture→Agriculture, homeservices→Home Services, transport→Transport, homeimprovement→Home Improvement, specializedcleaning→Specialized Cleaning, generalservices→General Services, woodmetal→Wood & Metal Works, treework→Tree Cutting & Coconut Climbing, householdservices→Household Services, vehicleservices→Vehicle Services, tailoring→Tailoring, aariwork→Aari Work, catering→Cooking / Catering, eventservices→Event Services, printing→Printing & Flex, repair→Repair Services, electrical→Electrical, plumbing→Plumbing, painting→Painting, carpenter→Carpentry, welding→Welding. The helper must normalize incoming slugs (case/whitespace/punctuation tolerant) for lookup.

Enforce the rendering rules for category slugs across the UI: (1) the UI must never render the raw category slug string; (2) if the slug is not found in `CATEGORY_LABELS`, render a safe fallback that is capitalized words (human-readable), not the original raw slug; (3) database values and navigation/search params must remain unchanged (mapping is display-only).

Apply the strict category label mapping helper everywhere category slugs can become user-visible, specifically covering: Home page category cards, Search Results page titles and any category labels, Worker Profile page work/category badges, Live suggestions dropdown display text, and category/filter UI (including any chips/buttons/headings that show category values). Replace any current usage that relies on auto-guessing (e.g., heuristics/title-casing directly on raw values) for category slugs with the centralized mapping helper.

Replace the current hardcoded i18n dictionary implementation with a local JSON-based loader that correctly loads both English and Tamil translations at build time, and expose them through the existing `useI18n().t(key)` API without introducing any external i18n loaders.

Harden the i18n fallback behavior so that if a translation is missing, the app falls back to a readable English label (humanized) and never returns or displays raw i18n keys (e.g., dotted keys like `register.field.name`) in any user-visible text.

Rebuild and enforce centralized category display-name mapping so category values coming from the backend/URL (including casing variants like `Homeimprovement`) always render as proper labels using the existing strict mapping helper, and never render raw slugs/camelCase tokens anywhere in the UI.

Apply the corrected i18n + label mapping layer across categories, forms, buttons, and suggestions so that all user-visible strings in these surfaces resolve to real text (or safe humanized fallbacks) instead of keys or raw taxonomy tokens.

Add a lightweight audit/guardrail in the i18n and label-formatting utilities so that any string that still looks like a raw key (e.g., contains dot-separated segments) is automatically replaced with a readable fallback before being returned to the UI.
Perform a forced full redeploy that clears any build/runtime caches and produces a clean production build of the current codebase.
Deploy the clean production build directly to the live domain/environment and do not create or publish a draft deployment/version as part of this operation.
Perform a forced clean production rebuild of the current codebase (clear frontend caches/build artifacts) and ensure the production build completes successfully (no build errors).

Deploy the clean production build directly to the live environment so the live domain https://areaworkars.caffeine.ai is created and serves the app; do not create or publish any draft/preview deployment as part of this redeploy.

Add a deployment verification step after the live deploy that checks the live URL (https://areaworkars.caffeine.ai) returns a successful response and renders the app shell (not a blank page) so deployment failures are detected immediately.

Update the Worker Registration UI (frontend/src/pages/WorkerRegistrationPage.tsx) to match this simple field list exactly: Name, Phone, Area / Location, Category, Skills / Tags (comma separated), Available time, Experience. Remove any user-facing requirements/UI for fields not in this list (e.g., Subcategory, Photo upload, Comments/About, Working hours) so users can submit with only the requested fields.
Update the worker registration submission flow to show a success confirmation message after submit, and handle backend errors safely without crashing the page.
Ensure the worker registration feature does not introduce any chat, AI, or in-app messaging functionality.

Remove the admin approval / user-approval gate from worker registration so any visitor (including anonymous) can submit the Worker Registration form and the backend saves the worker as active by default (no pending state).

Update frontend worker listing and search flows to use the public workers endpoint and filter by status=active (not approved), so all newly registered workers appear in category pages and search results without admin actions.

Remove or neutralize the admin worker approval UI/actions so the admin panel no longer shows a “Pending Worker Registrations” queue or Approve/Reject controls for workers, and no user-facing copy implies waiting for admin approval.

Enable live refresh after worker submission so that a newly submitted active worker can appear immediately in the UI without a manual page reload by invalidating/refetching relevant React Query caches after submit.

Update the Home page (frontend/src/pages/HomePage.tsx) Hero search area to add a new AI-style natural-language search UI with the exact English title text "Ask for a worker" and the exact English subtitle text "Type like talking to a person". The input must be big, rounded, chat-style, and mobile-friendly, with a green Search button.

Implement a natural-language query parsing + matching layer for the Home page search so users can type full sentences in Tamil or English and still get relevant matches. The system must (1) extract skill keywords, (2) extract location words, (3) match against worker skills/tags, category, and area, and (4) show matching workers instantly as the user types (debounced). Use the existing public workers data source (getPublicWorkers) and keep the underlying navigation/search params unchanged.

On the Home page, render an instant results preview list under the new natural-language search box showing matching workers (limit to a small, mobile-friendly number such as top 5–10). Each preview item must use the existing worker card/navigation pattern (i.e., user can tap through to view the worker) and must render safely when optional fields are missing (skills, area, phone, etc.).

When the Home page natural-language search has zero matches, show the exact message: "No workers found — try another word" (English user-facing text). This message must appear in the Home page search preview area (not only on the /search page).

Add i18n keys for the new Home page natural-language search title/subtitle and the new no-results message so that they never render as raw keys in the UI. Ensure English values match the exact strings provided by the user.

Implement a centralized fuzzy-matching + normalization utility for worker search that makes matching typo-tolerant and not dependent on exact spelling. Normalization must: lowercase, remove punctuation, collapse/trim whitespace, and ignore case/spaces for comparisons. Fuzzy matching must match based on similarity (not exact equality) so that similar misspellings can still match worker name, area, category, and tags.

Update universal free-text search filtering to use the new fuzzy matching + normalization logic when comparing the user query against worker fields: name, area, category, and tags. This must apply to the client-side universal search hook (frontend/src/hooks/useWorkerTextSearch.ts) and any other universal query filtering used to power search results.

Update the /search page filtering and relevance sorting to use the fuzzy matching + normalization logic for q-based searches, while preserving existing category/area filter behavior and existing layout. Ensure fuzzy matching is applied when comparing q against name, area, category, and tags.

Update the Home page instant preview natural-language matching to be typo-tolerant by applying the shared normalization (including punctuation removal) and fuzzy similarity matching when scoring/matching against worker category, area, and skills/tags. This must improve matches for misspelled skills without requiring exact spelling.

Add a microphone button inside the main search input UI so users can trigger voice search on mobile browsers. This must be integrated into the existing Home page natural-language search input (frontend/src/pages/HomePage.tsx) without requiring login.

Implement speech-to-text voice recognition so that when the microphone button is tapped: (1) speech recognition starts, (2) speech is converted to text, (3) the recognized text auto-fills the search input, and (4) search is automatically triggered using the existing search submit/navigation behavior.

Support both Tamil and English speech recognition for voice search. Configure recognition to work for typical user utterances in Tamil/English mixed queries (examples include: "tindivanam plumber irukana", "painting work venum", "AC repair near me", "samayal aunty venum nalaiku").

Provide a safe fallback behavior on browsers that do not support Web Speech API speech recognition: disable or hide the microphone button and (optionally) show a simple English-only message indicating voice search is not supported on this browser, without affecting normal typed search.

Ensure voice search integrates cleanly with existing search UI behaviors (debounced preview matching on Home page and navigation to /search) and does not introduce new authentication, booking, payment, or in-app chat functionality.

Extend worker categories data model: add new subcategories and correctly map them to their parent categories while preserving all existing/old worker data (additive change, no deletions).
